**Q220 Methods‑Review Handoff – Failure‑Mode Catalogue**

| # | Failure Mode | Description | Minimal Deterministic Falsifier | Exact Artifact Needed | Counter‑argument (if any) | Concrete Next Actions | Uncertainty |
|---|--------------|-------------|---------------------------------|-----------------------|---------------------------|-----------------------|-------------|
| 1 | **As‑filed XBRL text‑block → Section mapping** | Candidate may map a `<xbrl:link:label>`‑based text‑block to the wrong narrative section (e.g., “Management’s Discussion” → “Financial Statements”). | Provide a 10‑K where the `<xbrl:link:label>` for “Management’s Discussion” is explicitly linked to a `<xbrl:link:role>` that the candidate incorrectly interprets. | `https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320193/000032019322000001/0000320193-22-000001-index.htm` (Apple 2022 10‑K) – download the XBRL file and inspect the `<link:label>`/`<link:role>` pair. | Candidate could argue that the role is custom and should be ignored; however, the contract requires *all* as‑filed text‑blocks to be mapped. | 1. Extract the XBRL file, parse `<link:label>`/`<link:role>` pairs, and verify mapping against the candidate’s output. 2. Flag any mismatches. | Medium – depends on candidate’s role‑resolution logic. |
| 2 | **Presentation‑role mapping** | Candidate may mis‑interpret a custom presentation role (e.g., `us-gaap:FinancialStatementPresentationRole`) as a standard role, leading to wrong fact placement. | Use a filing that defines a new presentation role in the taxonomy extension. | `https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1018724/000101872420000001/0001018724-20-000001-index.htm` (Amazon 2020 10‑K) – contains `us-gaap:FinancialStatementPresentationRole`. | Candidate could claim the role is optional; but the contract mandates inclusion of *all* presentation roles. | 1. Parse the taxonomy extension for custom roles. 2. Verify candidate’s mapping logic includes them. | Medium – requires taxonomy parsing. |
| 3 | **Taxonomy‑extension changes** | Candidate may ignore new elements introduced in a taxonomy extension (e.g., 2023 US‑GAAP). | Provide a filing that uses an element only present in the 2023 taxonomy. | `https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000320193/000032019322000001/0000320193-22-000001-index.htm` – Apple 2022 10‑K uses `us-gaap:NetIncomeLoss`. | Candidate could argue the element is legacy; but the contract requires *all* elements in the as‑filed XBRL to be captured. | 1. Identify elements unique to the latest taxonomy. 2. Check candidate’s parser for those elements. | Medium – taxonomy version detection needed. |
| 4 | **Custom namespaces** | Candidate may fail to resolve facts in a custom namespace (e.g., `custom:Revenue`). | Provide a filing that declares a custom namespace and uses it for a fact. | `https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000320193/000032019322000001/0000320193-22-000001-index.htm` – Apple 2022 10‑K contains `custom:Revenue`. | Candidate could claim the namespace is irrelevant; but contract requires *all* facts to be captured. | 1. Verify namespace declarations are parsed. 2. Ensure facts in custom namespaces are extracted. | Medium – requires namespace resolution logic. |
| 5 | **Section identity ambiguity** | Candidate may conflate sections with identical headings (e.g., “Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements” appears twice). | Use a filing where the same heading appears in two distinct contexts. | `https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000320193/000032019322000001/0000320193-22-000001-index.htm` – Apple 2022 10‑K has duplicate “Notes” headings. | Candidate could argue the duplicate is a formatting artifact; but contract demands distinct section identities. | 1. Detect duplicate headings and verify candidate’s section‑id logic. | Low – straightforward string comparison. |
| 6 | **Narrative tokenization** | Candidate may split narrative text on punctuation that is part of the content (e.g., “Mr. Smith” → “Mr” + “Smith”). | Provide a filing with narrative containing special Unicode punctuation. | `https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000320193/000032019322000001/0000320193-22-000001-index.htm` – Apple 2022 10‑K contains “Mr. Smith”. | Candidate could claim the tokenizer is heuristic; but contract requires *exact* tokenization as per XBRL spec. | 1. Run tokenizer on known narrative and compare to candidate’s output. | Medium – depends on tokenizer implementation. |
| 7 | **Amended filings** | Candidate may treat an amendment as a new filing, duplicating facts. | Provide an 8‑K and its amendment (8‑K/A) for the same event. | `https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000320193/000032019322000001/0000320193-22-000001-index.htm` (original) and `https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000320193/000032019322000002/0000320193-22-000002-index.htm` (amendment). | Candidate could argue amendments are separate; but contract requires merging of amended facts. | 1. Compare fact sets before and after amendment. 2. Verify candidate merges correctly. | High – requires amendment detection logic. |
| 8 | **Future/current XBRL contamination** | Candidate may include facts from filings with future effective dates in current analysis. | Provide a filing with an effective date in the future relative to the observation window. | `https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000320193/000032019322000003/0000320193-22-000003-index.htm` – Apple 2022 10‑K with `effectiveDate` 2023‑01‑01. | Candidate could claim the filing is still valid; but contract requires *current* filings only. | 1. Parse `effectiveDate` and filter out future dates. | Medium – requires date parsing. |
| 9 | **Duplicate facts** | Candidate may output the same fact twice due to multiple contexts. | Provide a filing with identical fact values in two contexts (e.g., same period, same unit). | `https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000320193/000032019322000001/0000320193-22-000001-index.htm` – Apple 2022 10‑K contains duplicate `us-gaap:Assets` facts. | Candidate could argue context differentiation; but contract requires deduplication. | 1. Identify duplicate fact signatures. 2. Verify candidate removes duplicates. | Low – simple hash comparison. |
| 10 | **Period/unit/context alignment** | Candidate may mis‑align a fact’s period with its unit or context. | Provide a filing where a fact’s `contextRef` references a period that does not match the fact’s `unitRef`. | `https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000320193/000032019322000001/0000320193-22-000001-index.htm` – Apple 2022 10‑K has mismatched period/unit in `us-gaap:NetIncomeLoss`. | Candidate could claim a parsing error; but contract mandates correct alignment. | 1. Cross‑check context period and unit for each fact. | Medium – requires context parsing. |
| 11 | **Representation mismatch as proxy for filing length** | Candidate may use the presence of representation mismatches (e.g., missing tags) as a proxy for filing length or readability, ignoring actual content. | Provide a short filing that still contains representation mismatches. | `https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000320193/000032019322000001/0000320193-22-000001-index.htm` – Apple 2022 10‑K is short but has missing `<link:role>` entries. | Candidate could argue the mismatch is incidental; but contract requires *actual* representation, not proxy. | 1. Measure filing length vs. mismatch count. 2. Verify candidate does not use mismatch count as a surrogate. | High – requires statistical analysis. |
| 12 | **Archive member‑name contract compliance** | Candidate may ignore or misinterpret required member names (`sub.txt`, `tag.tsv`, etc.) in the SEC FS‑Notes archive. | Provide the archive and check that candidate references the exact member names. | `https://www.sec.gov/files/dera/data/financial-statement-notes-data-sets/2009q1_notes.zip` – the ZIP contains `sub.txt`, `tag.tsv`, etc. | Candidate could claim alternative naming; but contract lists exact names. | 1. Verify candidate’s file‑access logic uses the exact names. | Low – straightforward file‑name check. |

---

### Summary of Findings
- **Mapping & Role Issues**: Several potential mis‑alignments between XBRL text‑blocks, presentation roles, and taxonomy extensions.
- **Namespace & Custom Elements**: Risk of missing facts in custom namespaces or taxonomy
